editorialStandard: Themes describe cultural and economic associations, not NaijaDeals supply availability. Rankings and volume claims appear only where the cited source states them. Themes with no adequate fetched source carry reviewStatus needs-source.

countries.name: Benin
countries.introduction: Benin links a busy coastal port to cotton, pineapple and shea-producing hinterlands, with Cotonou handling trade for its landlocked neighbours. Commercial life runs through port corridors, crop processing and a growing garment sector that supplies regional and European buyers.

themes.label: Cotton
themes.association: Seed cotton grown across the northern belt and ginned for fibre; the WTO's trade policy review notes that cotton and its by-products dominate Benin's goods exports.

sources.title: Trade Policy Review: Benin (WT/TPR/S/362)

themes.label: Pineapple
themes.association: Fresh pineapple and juice from the Allada plateau; the Pain de Sucre variety has held a protected geographical indication since 2020, and national output is estimated at about 450,000 tonnes a year.

sources.title: Filière ananas – PACOFIDE

themes.label: Shea
themes.association: Shea kernels and butter collected and processed by rural women's groups in the north.

sources.title: Global Shea Alliance – about the shea industry

themes.label: Rice and maize
themes.association: Lowland rice and maize grown for household food and regional markets.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Benin

themes.label: Garments
themes.association: Cut-make-trim garment production that the World Bank includes in Benin's manufacturing base.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Benin

themes.label: Port and transit trade
themes.association: Cotonou's port, terminal and logistics services, which the World Bank describes as leading the service sector alongside trade and transport.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Benin

countries.name: Burkina Faso
countries.introduction: Burkina Faso is a landlocked Sahelian economy where gold and cotton anchor exports while millet, sorghum and livestock sustain rural households. Ouagadougou's craft fair has made the country a meeting point for West African artisans and buyers.

themes.label: Cotton
themes.association: Seed cotton ginned into fibre; SOFITEX reports handling about 80 percent of Burkina Faso's cotton production and paying growers each season.

sources.title: SOFITEX – Société Burkinabè des Fibres Textiles

themes.label: Gold
themes.association: Gold mining that the World Bank identifies as a driver of industry and a support to the external balance.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Burkina Faso

themes.label: Shea
themes.association: Shea kernels and butter collected and processed across the savannah parklands, a sector the Global Shea Alliance links to rural women's livelihoods.

sources.title: Global Shea Alliance – about the shea industry

themes.label: Craft industries
themes.association: Textiles, bronze, leather, basketry and jewellery shown at Ouagadougou's international craft fair, one of the continent's largest artisan gatherings.

sources.title: SIAO – Salon International de l'Artisanat de Ouagadougou

themes.label: Millet, sorghum and fonio
themes.association: Millet, sorghum, maize and fonio grown for household food and local markets, with coarse-grain prices closely watched.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Burkina Faso

themes.label: Livestock
themes.association: Cattle, sheep and goats raised across the Sahel, part of the agricultural economy the World Bank describes alongside farming.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Burkina Faso

countries.name: Cabo Verde
countries.introduction: Cabo Verde is an Atlantic archipelago whose economy leans on tourism, services and marine resources rather than large-scale farming. Smallholder coffee on Fogo and irrigated island horticulture show how scarce arable land is farmed carefully and intensively.

themes.label: Fogo coffee
themes.association: Arabica grown on Fogo's volcanic slopes between 350 and 1,300 metres, harvested from February, with current output a little over 100 tonnes a year.

sources.title: Café do Fogo: O Melhor do Mundo

themes.label: Island tourism
themes.association: Island tourism that the World Bank says employs more than two thirds of the population and contributes about a quarter of GDP.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Cabo Verde

themes.label: Blue economy
themes.association: Coastal and marine livelihoods supported through the World Bank's Resilient Tourism and Blue Economy Development Project.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Cabo Verde

themes.label: Horticulture and maize
themes.association: Irrigated vegetables, beans and maize grown in island valleys, where maize is virtually the only cereal.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Cabo Verde

themes.label: Renewable energy
themes.association: Solar and wind generation supported by the Renewable Energy and Improved Utility Performance Project.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Cabo Verde

themes.label: Export services
themes.association: Trade and investment facilitation for exporters of goods and services, provided by the national trade and investment agency.

sources.title: Cabo Verde TradeInvest – investment and export promotion

countries.name: Côte d'Ivoire
countries.introduction: Côte d'Ivoire is the world's largest cocoa producer and a major exporter of cashew, mango, shea and palm oil. Abidjan's port and processing industries turn these commodities into an export economy that also includes offshore hydrocarbons.

themes.label: Cocoa
themes.association: Cocoa beans from the world's leading producer, with processing into butter, liquor and powder.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Côte d'Ivoire

themes.label: Cashew
themes.association: Raw cashew nuts and kernels, with processed exports reported above 30 percent of production.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Côte d'Ivoire

themes.label: Mango
themes.association: Mangoes supported under an agricultural value-chain project that also covers shea and palm oil.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Côte d'Ivoire

themes.label: Shea
themes.association: Shea kernels and butter from the northern savannah, part of a value-chain programme with mango and palm oil.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Côte d'Ivoire

themes.label: Palm oil
themes.association: Palm oil produced for regional and international markets.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Côte d'Ivoire

themes.label: Oil and gas
themes.association: Offshore oil and gas that the World Bank describes as an expanding industry.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Côte d'Ivoire

countries.name: Gambia
countries.introduction: The Gambia follows the river of the same name, with groundnuts, rice and horticulture supporting most rural livelihoods. Coastal tourism, artisanal fisheries and a small manufacturing base add earnings beyond the single river corridor that defines the country.

themes.label: Groundnuts
themes.association: Groundnuts bought and traded through the national food-security corporation, which reports more than 100,000 tonnes purchased in recent seasons.

sources.title: National Food Security, Processing and Marketing Corporation (NFSPMC)

themes.label: Cashew
themes.association: Cashew orchards supported under an agricultural value-chains project.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: The Gambia

themes.label: Rice
themes.association: Rice and maize grown along the river, with government seed distribution and a sustainable rice and millet food-systems project.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Gambia

themes.label: Horticulture
themes.association: Vegetables and fruit for hotels, urban markets and export, listed among The Gambia's agricultural value chains.

sources.title: Invest in Agribusiness in The Gambia
World Bank country overview: The Gambia

themes.label: Fisheries and aquaculture
themes.association: Artisanal and coastal fisheries plus aquaculture, identified by the investment agency as a priority value chain.

sources.title: Invest in Agribusiness in The Gambia

themes.label: Tourism
themes.association: Coastal and river tourism; the World Bank reports arrivals rising 5.4 percent to 120,713 in the first half of 2026.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: The Gambia

countries.name: Ghana
countries.introduction: Ghana combines cocoa, gold and oil exports with a broad non-traditional export sector that includes shea, pineapple, seafood and handwoven cloth. Accra and Kumasi anchor trade, processing and a growing creative-industry supply chain serving regional and international buyers.

themes.label: Cocoa
themes.association: Cocoa beans regulated and marketed through the national cocoa board, which sets the producer price and publishes purchases and exports by destination.

sources.title: Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD)

themes.label: Fugu and handwoven cloth
themes.association: Handwoven fugu smock from the northern regions, which the export authority promotes as a heritage textile for international buyers.

sources.title: Fugu: Preserving Heritage, Promoting Exports

themes.label: Shea
themes.association: Shea kernels and butter processed mainly by women's cooperatives, a sector the Global Shea Alliance supports across West Africa.

sources.title: Global Shea Alliance – about the shea industry

themes.label: Gold
themes.association: Gold exports that the World Bank identifies as supporting a current account surplus.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Ghana

themes.label: Pineapple
themes.association: Pineapple grown for processing, packaging and sale at home and abroad.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Ghana

themes.label: Fisheries
themes.association: Marine and inland fisheries listed among the export authority's priority sectors.

sources.title: Ghana Export Promotion Authority

countries.name: Guinea
countries.introduction: Guinea holds some of the world's largest bauxite reserves and is adding iron ore from Simandou to a mining economy long centred on Conakry's port. Agriculture, including rice, maize and fonio, remains the largest employer.

themes.label: Bauxite
themes.association: Bauxite that APIP says accounts for about a quarter of world reserves, with export volumes up 31 percent year on year in the first half of 2025.

sources.title: APIP – Agence de Promotion des Investissements Privés
World Bank country overview: Guinea

themes.label: Iron ore
themes.association: Iron ore from Simandou, which the World Bank says is ramping up exports and driving mining growth.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Guinea
APIP – Agence de Promotion des Investissements Privés

themes.label: Gold
themes.association: Gold within a mining portfolio that APIP lists alongside bauxite, iron ore, diamonds and rare minerals.

sources.title: APIP – Agence de Promotion des Investissements Privés

themes.label: Fonio
themes.association: Fonio, the ancient cereal that the World Bank lists among promoted agricultural exports.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Guinea

themes.label: Rice and maize
themes.association: Rice and maize grown in lowlands and uplands, part of the agropastoral sector described in the FAO brief.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Guinea

themes.label: Hydropower
themes.association: Hydropower potential that APIP highlights alongside mining and agriculture.

sources.title: APIP – Agence de Promotion des Investissements Privés

countries.name: Guinea-Bissau
countries.introduction: Guinea-Bissau's export economy rests heavily on raw cashew nuts, grown by smallholders across the mainland. Rice, coarse grains and coastal fisheries support daily life around the Bijagós archipelago and the country's river estuaries and island communities.

themes.label: Cashew
themes.association: Raw cashew nuts that the World Bank calls the main export driver, with a strong 2025 harvest.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Guinea-Bissau

themes.label: Rice
themes.association: Rice grown in lowland and irrigated systems, one of the country's two main cereal groups.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Guinea-Bissau

themes.label: Maize, millet and sorghum
themes.association: Maize, millet and sorghum grown alongside rice for household food.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Guinea-Bissau

themes.label: Fisheries
themes.association: Artisanal and industrial fishing managed under the Ministry of Fisheries, whose statistics report 245 licences, 234 vessels and a January biological rest period.

sources.title: Ministério das Pescas – Guiné-Bissau

themes.label: Bijagós ecotourism
themes.association: Visits across the Bolama-Bijagós Biosphere Reserve and other protected areas, guided through the national biodiversity institute.

sources.title: Ecoturismo – IBAP Guiné-Bissau

themes.label: Services
themes.association: Services, which the World Bank names alongside agriculture as a key growth driver for Guinea-Bissau.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Guinea-Bissau

countries.name: Liberia
countries.introduction: Liberia's economy is shaped by rubber, iron ore, gold and timber, with Monrovia as the main port and commercial centre. Rice farming and tree crops such as cocoa support rural households alongside these extractive and plantation sectors.

themes.label: Rubber
themes.association: Natural rubber from plantations and smallholder tapping, one of Liberia's named exports.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Liberia

themes.label: Iron ore
themes.association: Iron ore mining and export, one of the commodities the World Bank names in Liberia's export base.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Liberia

themes.label: Gold
themes.association: Gold, which the World Bank lists among Liberia's exports.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Liberia

themes.label: Timber
themes.association: Timber and value-added wood products from Liberia's forests.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Liberia

themes.label: Rice
themes.association: Paddy rice, with about 322,000 tonnes produced in 2025 and irrigated lowland development in Lofa, Nimba and Bong.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Liberia

themes.label: Cocoa
themes.association: Cocoa planting and tree-crop extension promoted by the Ministry of Agriculture.

sources.title: Ministry of Agriculture – Republic of Liberia

countries.name: Mali
countries.introduction: Mali is a landlocked Sahelian country where gold and cotton dominate formal exports while millet, sorghum and rice support most households. Bamako and Ségou also sustain artisan textiles, including bogolan, alongside livestock herding and river fishing.

themes.label: Cotton
themes.association: Seed cotton ginned and marketed through Mali's national cotton company, which describes cotton as an engine of the national economy.

sources.title: CMDT – Compagnie Malienne pour le Développement des Textiles
World Bank country overview: Mali

themes.label: Gold
themes.association: Gold, which the World Bank identifies among Mali's main exports.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Mali

themes.label: Lithium
themes.association: Lithium, an emerging mineral export that the World Bank lists alongside gold and cotton.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Mali

themes.label: Millet and sorghum
themes.association: Millet and sorghum grown for household food, with coarse-grain prices monitored through the season.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Mali

themes.label: Rice
themes.association: Rice grown alongside other cereals, a staple the FAO brief tracks through the season.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Mali

themes.label: Bogolan
themes.association: Mud-dyed cotton cloth decorated with clay and plant tannins, documented in a WIPO presentation on geographical indications and traditional knowledge for Bogolan.

sources.title: Indications géographiques, savoirs traditionnels et expressions culturelles traditionnelles : cas du Bogolan

countries.name: Mauritania
countries.introduction: Mauritania pairs iron ore and gold mining with an Atlantic fishing zone extending across 234,000 square kilometres. Pastoral livestock, desert tourism and emerging gas production round out an economy concentrated in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou.

themes.label: Iron ore
themes.association: Iron ore that anchors Mauritania's mining exports, with SNIM reporting a 27 percent contribution to export volume.

sources.title: SNIM – Société Nationale Industrielle et Minière
APIM – Agence de Promotion des Investissements en Mauritanie

themes.label: Fisheries
themes.association: Octopus, sardinella and other catch from a 234,000 square kilometre exclusive economic zone along 750 kilometres of Atlantic coast.

sources.title: APIM – Agence de Promotion des Investissements en Mauritanie
World Bank country overview: Mauritania

themes.label: Livestock
themes.association: Camel, cattle, sheep and goat herding, with APIM reporting more than 30 million head of livestock.

sources.title: APIM – Agence de Promotion des Investissements en Mauritanie

themes.label: Gold and copper
themes.association: Gold and copper mining alongside iron ore, both named in APIM's mining sector.

sources.title: APIM – Agence de Promotion des Investissements en Mauritanie
World Bank country overview: Mauritania

themes.label: Natural gas
themes.association: Offshore gas from the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim field, which the World Bank identifies as a new export stream.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Mauritania

themes.label: Tourism
themes.association: Desert, coastal and heritage tourism promoted by the investment agency.

sources.title: APIM – Agence de Promotion des Investissements en Mauritanie

countries.name: Niger
countries.introduction: Niger is a vast Sahelian country whose exports are dominated by uranium, oil and gold, moved through neighbouring corridors. Millet, sorghum and irrigated rice support households, while livestock herding connects pastoral communities to regional markets.

themes.label: Uranium
themes.association: Uranium, long one of Niger's principal mineral exports.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Niger

themes.label: Oil
themes.association: Crude oil production and pipeline exports, which the World Bank names among Niger's exports.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Niger

themes.label: Gold
themes.association: Gold, part of the mineral base the World Bank describes alongside uranium and oil.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Niger

themes.label: Livestock
themes.association: Pastoral livestock herding, one of the priority sectors listed by the investment agency.

sources.title: ANPIPS – Agence Nigérienne de la Promotion des Investissements Privés et des Projets Stratégiques

themes.label: Irrigated farming
themes.association: Irrigated farming in river valleys, which the World Bank highlights within Niger's agricultural economy.

sources.title: World Bank country overview: Niger

themes.label: Millet and sorghum
themes.association: Millet and sorghum, the rain-fed cereals that dominate household food in the Sahel.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS country brief: Niger

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.introduction: Nigeria's economy spans oil and gas alongside cocoa, sesame, cashew and leather exports. Lagos and Kano anchor commerce and manufacturing, while textile crafts such as adire remain part of the country's cultural and commercial identity.

themes.label: Cocoa
themes.association: Cocoa beans and processed products, one of the product profiles the export council publishes for buyers.

countries.name: Senegal
countries.introduction: Senegal's export profile combines seafood, mangoes, processed foods and handicrafts with gold and newly produced hydrocarbons. Dakar concentrates the country's port, services and manufacturing activity, while irrigated horticulture reaches regional and European markets through the year.

themes.label: Mango
themes.association: Fresh mangoes, one of the product groups the export agency promotes in its market sheets.

sources.title: ASEPEX – Agence Sénégalaise de Promotion des Exportations

countries.name: Sierra Leone
countries.introduction: Sierra Leone's exports centre on rutile, diamonds, bauxite and iron ore, with Freetown as the main port. Rice remains the staple crop, and coastal fisheries and tourism offer additional livelihoods along the country's long Atlantic shoreline.

themes.association: Rutile, one of the minerals the World Bank names in Sierra Leone's export base.

countries.name: Togo
countries.introduction: Togo's economy pivots on Lomé's deep-water port and regional corridor trade, with phosphate, cotton and agro-food exports alongside. The narrow territory links coastal manufacturing and free-zone activity to an inland northern cotton and shea-producing savannah.

themes.label: Phosphate
themes.association: Phosphate rock, with the national company reporting average output of about 1.1 million tonnes a year.

sources.title: SNPT – Société Nouvelle des Phosphates du Togo

themes.label: Port and corridor logistics
themes.association: Lomé's deep-water port and regional corridor services, which the World Bank highlights in Togo's transport and logistics sector.
